items.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: Doing the great songs of like Cole Porter, George Gershwin and Jerome Kern

ctx.x: Do you think it helped also that your vocals were using — they weren’t singing the lyrics so that there was no language thing there?

Oh yeah. You hit on something that I usually bring out in an interview when I talk about that first album, and they usually say, “what do you think made your albums successful?” And I think that was one of the things. I didn’t have any language barrier. And when Columbia Records sent samples out all over the world, that original “S’ Wonderful” album was picked up all over the world and became quite popular all over the world, as did a lot of the follow up albums. And that was one of the things. Doing the great…
Did you start to hear some imitators? © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-
